claim: H4K31ac was identified by mass spectrometry in T. gondii nucleosomes.
source: While studying the protein content of nucleosomes from T. gondii-infected cells, we and others mapped an acetylation site on histone H4 lysine 31 (H4K31ac) that had previously been largely underestimated (Figure 1a) (Jeffers and Sullivan, 2012; Xue et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1a and cited references.

claim: H4K31ac was identified in both the proteome and acetylome of P. falciparum throughout the intraerythrocytic developmental cycle.
source: This modification was also identified in both the proteome (Saraf et al., 2016) and acetylome (Cobbold et al., 2016) of P. falciparum throughout the intraerythrocytic developmental cycle of the parasite.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The H4K31 residue is located at the N-terminus of the H4 α1 helix with its side chain extended in the major groove of DNA.
source: The H4K31 residue is located at the N-terminus of the H4 α1 helix and its side chain is extended in the major groove of the DNA (Figure 1b and c).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 1b and c.

claim: Acetylation of H4K31 abolishes its interaction with DNA mediated by a water molecule.
source: The addition of an acetyl group to the -NH2 group of the lysine side chain (K31) abolishes its interaction with DNA mediated by a water molecule (Figure 1c, right panel).
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis and inference from the chemical properties of acetylation.

claim: The H4K31 residue is well conserved across species.
source: Although the H4K31 residue is well conserved across species (Figure 1b), mass spectrometry initially indicates that its acetylation is restricted to metazoans, as an unexpected mark in inflammatory and auto-immune contexts (Garcia et al., 2005; Soldi et al., 2014), as it was found neither in yeast nor in the ciliated protozoan Tetrahymena (Garcia et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence alignment data in Figure 1b and citations.

claim: H4K31ac was initially thought to be restricted to metazoans and not found in yeast or Tetrahymena.
source: Although the H4K31 residue is well conserved across species (Figure 1b), mass spectrometry initially indicates that its acetylation is restricted to metazoans, as an unexpected mark in inflammatory and auto-immune contexts (Garcia et al., 2005; Soldi et al., 2014), as it was found neither in yeast nor in the ciliated protozoan Tetrahymena (Garcia et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous mass spectrometry studies.

claim: Recent studies show that H4K31ac also arises in the Apicomplexa phylum.
source: Recent studies, including our present findings, contradict this view as they show that this PTM also arises in the Apicomplexa phylum (Cobbold et al., 2016; Jeffers and Sullivan, 2012; Saraf et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to recent studies and the current study's findings.

claim: H4K31ac is distributed exclusively and uniformly within the nuclei of both parasite and human cells.
source: Using human primary fibroblasts infected by T. gondii, we found H4K31ac to be distributed exclusively and uniformly within the nuclei of both parasite and human cells (Figure 1d).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: Exposing cells to FR235222 HDACi significantly increased H4K31ac signal intensity in parasite nucleosomes.
source: We also found that exposing cells to a histone deacetylase inhibitor (HDACi), e.g., FR235222, significantly increased H4K31ac signal intensity, which is otherwise moderate in parasite nucleosomes (Figure 1e).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: FR235222 treatment increased H4K31ac signal intensity but did not alter H3K14ac and H3K27ac levels.
source: Interestingly, PTMs at histone H3 tails, for example at H3K14ac and H3K27ac, were not altered upon FR235222 treatment under our conditions, which contrasts with the increased signal of H4K31ac and further confirms the specificity of the H4K31ac-directed antibodies (Figure 2b).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: H4K31ac showed a nuclear punctate pattern in P. falciparum, reminiscent of active loci clusters in specialized 'transcription factories'.
source: Overall, H4K31ac showed a nuclear punctate pattern, reminiscent of active loci clusters in specialized 'transcription factories' (Figure 3b) (Mancio-Silva and Scherf, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 3b and a citation.

claim: H4K31ac is scattered through the nucleoplasm of MEFs but excluded from nucleoli and segregated away from heterochromatic foci.
source: H4K31ac was observed scattered through the nucleoplasm of MEFs but excluded from nucleoli and segregated away from heterochromatic foci, as were the transcription-associated PTMs H3K4ac, H3K9ac and H3K27ac (Figure 3d).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: H4K31ac displays an euchromatic pattern in both metazoans and apicomplexans.
source: Taken together, these experiments show that H4K31ac displays an euchromatic pattern in both metazoans and apicomplexans.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the immunofluorescence data presented.

claim: Cyclopeptide HDACi strongly enhanced H4K31ac levels in parasite nuclei.
source: We found that cyclopeptide HDACi strongly enhanced H4K31ac levels in parasite nuclei, whereas other inhibitors had no effect (Figure 4a and b).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4a and b.

claim: Inactivation of TgHDAC3 caused hyperacetylation of H4K31 in parasite nuclei.
source: Inactivation of TgHDAC3 but not of other TgHDAC genes caused hyperacetylation of H4K31 in parasite nuclei (Figure 5a,b and c), thereby mimicking the effect of the cyclic tetrapeptide HDACi on the enzyme (Figure 4) (Bougdour et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by CRISPR-mediated gene disruption data shown in Figure 5.

claim: TgGCN5b is an H4K31 acetyltransferase.
source: Altogether these data clearly identify TgGCN5b as an H4K31 acetyltransferase whose activity is counteracted by TgHDAC3.
evidence: The claim is based on CRISPR-mediated gene disruption experiments showing that TgGCN5b depletion reduces H4K31ac.

claim: Cas9-mediated gene disruption of HAT1 had no effect on H4K31 acetylation.
source: However, cas9-mediated gene disruption of HAT1 had no effect on H4K31 acetylation (Figure 6a and b), and TgGCN5b was the only HAT-encoding gene whose disruption resulted in a drastic drop in H4K31ac signals in the parasite nuclei (Figure 6a and b).
evidence: The claim is supported by CRISPR-mediated gene disruption data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Depletion of TgGCN5b led to a reduction of both H3K14ac and H4K31ac signals in vivo.
source: Furthermore, we noticed that the amino acid sequence surrounding H4K31 was not homologous to the preferred GCN5 consensus sites of acetylation found at H3K14 (Kuo et al., 1996) or H3K36 (Morris et al., 2007), yet the depletion of TgGCN5b led to a reduction of both H3K14ac (Figure 6c and d) and H4K31ac (Figure 6a and b) signals in vivo, suggesting that the repertoire of the lysine residues being acetylated by the GCN5 family is more diverse in T. gondii than in other organisms.
evidence: The claim is supported by CRISPR-mediated gene disruption data and citations.

claim: H4K31me1 appeared to be uniformly distributed within the nucleus of dividing parasites but no signal was detected in the nucleus of the infected human cell.
source: In situ, the H4K31me1 modification appeared to be uniformly distributed within the nucleus of dividing parasites, but surprisingly no signal was detected in the nucleus of the infected human cell (Figure 7a), although this PTM had been previously detected by mass spectrometry in human samples (Garcia et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7a and a citation.

claim: H4K31me1 was not (or barely) detected in interphase nuclei of quiescent infected HFFs or uninfected MEFs, but it decorated mitotic chromosomes.
source: H4K31me1 was not (or barely) detected in interphase nuclei of either quiescent infected HFFs (Figure 7a) or uninfected MEFs (Figure 7b), but it decorated mitotic chromosomes , providing even more pronounced signals in the chromosome arms than the usual mitotic marker H3S10 phosphorylation (Figure 7b).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7a and 7b.

claim: H4K31me1 may have a role during cell division in mammalian cells.
source: These observations argue for a possible role for H4K31 methylation during cell division in mammalian cells.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that H4K31me1 decorates mitotic chromosomes.

claim: In P. falciparum, H4K31me1 displayed a peculiar condensed punctate pattern similar to that of the H3K9me3 mark at the nuclear periphery.
source: In P. falciparum, H4K31me1 displayed a peculiar condensed punctate pattern (Figure 7c), similar to that of the H3K9me3 mark (Lopez-Rubio et al., 2009) at the nuclear periphery, which is reminiscent of clustering of heterochromatin/subtelomeric regions (Freitas-Junior et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7c and citations.

claim: H4K31ac and H4K31me1 exhibited distinct patterns of enrichment across T. gondii chromosomes and were mutually exclusive genome-wide.
source: Visual display of the chromosomal distribution indicated that H4K31ac and H4K31me1 exhibited distinct patterns of enrichment across the chromosomes and were mutually exclusive genome-wide (e.g., Chr. Ib, Figure 8a).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 8a.

claim: H4K31ac was enriched in distinct peaks at intergenic regions, with 75% mapping outside the gene body.
source: Zooming in to detailed gene level revealed that H4K31ac was enriched in distinct peaks at intergenic regions (IGRs) (Figure 8b), of which 75% mapped outside the gene body (Figure 8c), in line with the euchromatic in situ localization (Figure 1 and Figure 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 8b and 8c.

claim: The calculated average profile of H4K31ac showed a pattern strikingly similar to that of H3K14ac and H3K4me3, characterized by high signals at 5'UTR/promoter that drop sharply after the translational initiation site.
source: The calculated average profile of H4K31ac showed a pattern strikingly similar to that of H3K14ac and H3K4me3, characterized by high signals at 5'UTR/promoter that drop sharply after the translational initiation site (Figure 8d).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq average profile data shown in Figure 8d.

claim: H4K31me1 showed a distinct pattern of enrichment spanning from the ATG to the entire gene body and absent from IGRs.
source: Conversely, H4K31me1 showed a distinct pattern of enrichment, best discernable at large genes, spanning from the ATG to the entire gene body (Figure 8b) and absent from IGRs (Figure 8c).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 8b and 8c.

claim: H4K31me1 is a novel PTM whose spreading was restricted to gene bodies in T. gondii.
source: Remarkably, these data allowed the identification of H4K31me1 as a novel PTM whose spreading was restricted to gene bodies in T. gondii (Figure 8b and d).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 8b and 8d.

claim: High mRNA level was associated with a high level of H4K31ac upstream of the ATG together with an enrichment along the gene body, which coincided with the expected lack of H4K31me1.
source: High mRNA level (in Q1, which includes the GRA1, MAG1 and SRS genes) was associated with a high level of H4K31ac upstream of the ATG together with an enrichment along the gene body, which coincided with the expected lack of H4K31me1 (Figure 9e and f).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data shown in Figure 9e and 9f.

claim: Moderate mRNA levels related to a relatively high level of H4K31me1 in the gene body and a restricted mapping of H4K31ac at the promoter, arguing for an inverse correlation between the yield of expression and the level of H4K31 methylation.
source: Strikingly, moderate mRNA levels (in Q2 and Q3, which include TGME49_233490 or TGME49_270230) related to a relatively high level of H4K31me1 in the gene body and a restricted mapping of H4K31ac at the promoter, thereby arguing for an inverse correlation between the yield of expression and the level of H4K31 methylation (Figure 9e and f).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data shown in Figure 9e and 9f.

claim: Transcriptionally repressed genes clustered in Q4 showed no significant enrichment of either H4K31ac or H4K31me1 but were enriched in the repressive mark H3K9me3.
source: Finally, transcriptionally repressed genes clustered in Q4 showed no significant enrichment of either H4K31ac or H4K31me1 (Figure 9e and f) but were enriched in the repressive mark H3K9me3 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 9e, 9f, and Figure 9—figure supplement 1e.

claim: ENO1 and BAG1 genes, which are expressed distinctively in the bradyzoite stage, were highly enriched in the repressive mark H3K9me3 but also unexpectedly enriched in the gene activation hallmark H3K14ac.
source: As such, the ENO1 and BAG1 genes, which are well known to be expressed distinctively in the bradyzoite stage during the chronic phase of infection (Pittman et al., 2014), were highly enriched in the repressive mark H3K9me3 but they were also unexpectedly enriched in the gene activation hallmark H3K14ac (Figure 10a and Figure 10—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 10a and Figure 10—figure supplement 1a, and a citation.

claim: The co-enrichment of H3K9me3 and H3K14ac was restricted to transcriptional units that become active in the sexual stages.
source: The co-enrichment of H3K9me3 and H3K14ac was somehow restricted to the transcriptional units that become active in the sexual stages (shown in red, Figure 10b).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 10b.

claim: H3K14ac and H3K9me3 could form bivalent chromatin domains capable of silencing developmental genes while keeping them poised for rapid activation upon cell differentiation.
source: Thus, H3K14ac and H3K9me3 could form the so-called bivalent chromatin domain capable of silencing developmental genes while keeping them poised for rapid activation upon cell differentiation (Voigt et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observed co-enrichment of H3K14ac and H3K9me3 at stage-specific genes, supported by a citation.

claim: H4K31me1 enrichment should allow this mark to predict unannotated genes explicitly, even when the low level of expression impedes detection by RNA profiling.
source: These features should allow this mark to predict unannotated genes explicitly, even when the low level of expression impedes detection by RNA profiling (Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: H4K31me1 was occasionally found to be enriched in chromosomal regions devoid of any predicted protein-coding genes, correlating with extensive transcription of large RNA transcripts reminiscent of long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs).
source: Although H4K31me1 rarely covered IGRs (Figure 8c), the mark was occasionally found to be enriched in chromosomal regions that were devoid of any predicted protein-coding genes (Figure 10d and Figure 10—figure supplement 5). This enrichment correlated with extensive transcription of large RNA transcripts, ranging from 20 to 70 kB, reminiscent of long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) in other eukaryotic cells (Azzalin and Lingner, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data shown in Figure 10d and Figure 10—figure supplement 5, and a citation.

claim: H4K31ac displayed a rather even distribution throughout the P. falciparum genome, like the euchromatic mark H3K4me3.
source: Like the euchromatic mark H3K4me3, H4K31ac displayed a rather even distribution throughout the genome (Figure 11a and enhanced view at Figure 11—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 11a and Figure 11—figure supplement 2.

claim: The distribution of H4K31ac in P. falciparum matched with the gene annotation, with high acetylation rates at promoters and low rates at the gene body of active genes.
source: As for T. gondii, the distribution of H4K31ac in P. falciparum matched with the gene annotation, i.e., high acetylation rates at promoters and low rates at the gene body of active genes (e.g., GAPDH, Figure 11b).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 11b.

claim: The presence of H4K31ac and that of the repressive mark H3K9me3 were inversely correlated in P. falciparum.
source: Consistent with this, the presence of H4K31ac and that of the repressive mark H3K9me3 were inversely correlated (Figure 11a).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 11a.

claim: H4K31me1 was remarkably enriched at pericentromeric regions that flank the cenH3-enriched centromeres in P. falciparum.
source: Although our ChIP-seq analysis confirmed the absence of pericentric enrichment of both H3K9me3 and HP1, it clearly highlighted a remarkable enrichment of H4K31me1 at pericentromeric regions that flank the cenH3-enriched centromeres (Figure 11d, Figure 11—figure supplement 3 and Figure 12a).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 11d, Figure 11—figure supplement 3, and Figure 12a.

claim: H4K31me1 may constrain PfCENH3 to the centromeres in P. falciparum, replacing the H3K9me3–HP1 functions described in most species.
source: It is therefore possible that H4K31me1 constrains PfCENH3 to the centromeres in P. falciparum, thus replacing the H3K9me3–HP1 functions described in most species.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observed enrichment of H4K31me1 at pericentromeric regions.

claim: H4K31me1 was also enriched at a few subtelomeric regions and more specifically at the telomere-associated repetitive element (TARE) repeat blocks shown to encode lncRNAs.
source: In addition to the pericentromeric localization, H4K31me1 was also enriched at a few subtelomeric regions and more specifically at the telomere-associated repetitive element (TARE, Figure 12b) repeat blocks shown to encode lncRNAs (Figure 12c) (Sierra-Miranda et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 12b and 12c, and a citation.

claim: H4K31me1 is a novel hallmark of heterochromatin in P. falciparum, but this mark is not similar to H3K9me3–HP1 in subtelomeric regions and at var genes.
source: The presence of the mark at pericentric chromatin combined with its absence at transcriptionally permissive loci (e.g. GAPDH, Figure 11b) suggest H4K31me1 as a novel hallmark of heterochromatin in P. falciparum, but this mark is not similar to H3K9me3–HP1 in subtelomeric regions and at var genes.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on ChIP-seq data showing the distribution of H4K31me1.

claim: Acetylation of H4K31 was predicted to trigger substantial conformational changes in the nucleosome by causing the loss of water-mediated interactions that K31 establishes with DNA and residue R35.
source: Its acetylation was predicted to trigger substantial conformational changes in the nucleosome by shifting the side chain of lysine from the unacetylated to the acetylated state, causing the loss of the water-mediated interactions that K31 establishes with DNA and the residue R35 (Figure 1c).
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis and inference from the chemical properties of acetylation.

claim: X-ray crystallography did not indicate large structural changes to nucleosomes when glutamine was substituted for lysine to mimic the acetylated state (H4Q31).
source: However, this prediction was not validated as X-ray crystallography did not indicate large structural changes to nucleosomes when glutamine was substituted for lysine to mimic the acetylated state (H4Q31, Figure 1c) (Iwasaki et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a structural study.

claim: H4K31ac may increase DNA unwrapping at the entry-exit point of the nucleosome, giving access to ATP-dependent chromatin remodelers.
source: Alternatively, H4K31ac may increase DNA unwrapping at the entry-exit point of the nucleosome, thus giving access to the ATP-dependent chromatin remodelers that act on nucleosome disassembly and turnover as proposed by Chatterjee et al. (2015).
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on a citation to a proposed mechanism.

claim: In T. gondii, H4K31ac relieves nucleosomal repression thus facilitating the access of the transcriptional machinery to the DNA template.
source: H4K31ac relieves nucleosomal repression thus facilitating the access of the transcriptional machinery to the DNA template, whereas H4K31 monomethylation probably locks the nucleosome in a repressed conformation that maintains chromatin in a closed or semi-closed state also called poised-state, while it also prevents GCN5-related HAT from catalyzing the acetylation of the residue.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observed genome-wide distribution of H4K31ac and H4K31me1.

claim: H4K31me1 enrichment only in the transcribed coding sequence of a subset of genes is typically associated with limited activity of the RNA polymerase II.
source: Interestingly, apart from its predicted effects on the nucleosome mobility and chromatin state, we found that, in T. gondii,H4K31ac also prevents methylation at the body of highly expressed genes, thereby ensuring maximal efficacy of the RNA polymerase progression and activity. Indeed, we found H4K31me1 enrichment only in the transcribed coding sequence of a subset of genes typically associated with limited activity of the RNA polymerase II.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data showing the correlation between H4K31me1 and gene expression levels.

claim: H4K31me1 may slow down RNA Pol II processing along the fiber and thus reduce the level of transcription by stabilizing the wrapping of DNA around the histone octamer.
source: In a model where the nucleosome disassembles in front of transcribing RNA polymerase II to allow its physical progression across transcribed units, it is plausible that, by stabilizing the wrapping of DNA around the histone octamer, H4K31me1 slows down RNA Pol II processing along the fiber and thus reduces the level of transcription.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the observed inverse correlation between H4K31me1 and gene expression.

claim: In budding yeast, H4K31 along with two proximal residues on the side of the nucleosome (H4R36 and H3L61) promotes the recruitment of the yFACT subunit Spt16 across transcribed genes.
source: In budding yeast, H4K31 along with two proximal residues on the side of the nucleosome (i.e., H4R36 and H3L61) promotes the recruitment of the yFACT subunit Spt16 across transcribed genes, as assessed by the typical change in Spt16 distribution in which occupancy shifts toward the 3' ends of transcribed genes in the H4K31E yeast mutant (Nguyen et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a study in budding yeast.

claim: Ubiquitylation of H4K31 has been reported as an additional regulatory PTM for transcription elongation in human cells.
source: The versatility of H4K31 goes beyond even these modifications as ubiquitylation of H4K31 has been reported as an additional regulatory PTM for transcription elongation in human cells (Kim et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a study in human cells.

claim: Blocking H4K31 ubiquitylation by K31R mutation markedly reduces H3K4 and H3K79 methylation and consequently impairs gene transcription.
source: Importantly, blocking H4K31 ubiquitylation by K31R mutation markedly reduces H3K4 and H3K79 methylation and consequently impairs gene transcription (Kim et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a study in human cells.

claim: Engineered budding yeast with H4K31 substitutions did not significantly affect cell viability but led to an unexpected increase of telomeric and ribosomal DNA silencing.
source: Engineered budding yeast with those substitutions did not significantly affect cell viability but led to an unexpected increase of telomeric and ribosomal DNA silencing (Hyland et al., 2005), both of which argue for the mutations' driving a non-permissive chromatin state.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a study in budding yeast.

claim: Glutamic acid (E) that mimics succinylated lysine was shown to compromise the growth in budding yeast severely.
source: In sharp contrast with the aforementioned substitutions, glutamic acid (E) that mimics succinylated lysine was shown to compromise the growth in budding yeast severely (Xie et al., 2012), maybe as a consequence of the alteration in the distribution of Spt16 across yeast genes (Nguyen et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies in budding yeast.

claim: Succinylation on H4K31 has been detected by mass spectrometry in T. gondii.
source: Succinylation on H4K31 has also been detected by mass spectrometry in T. gondii (Li et al., 2014; Nardelli et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to mass spectrometry studies.

claim: H4K31 methylation would counteract the activating effect of H4K31 acetylation and succinylation by preventing the nucleosome from adopting an open conformation that permits gene expression.
source: In this context, H4K31 methylation would counteract the activating effect of H4K31 acetylation and succinylation, by preventing the nucleosome from adopting an open conformation that permits gene expression.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observed mutually exclusive distribution of H4K31ac and H4K31me1.

claim: P. falciparum heterochromatin was originally defined by increased nucleosomal occupancy, histone deacetylation, H3K9me3 and the binding of PfHP1.
source: Originally, P. falciparum heterochromatin — in which clusters of genes are maintained in a silent state — was singularly defined by increased nucleosomal occupancy, histone deacetylation, H3K9me3 and the binding of PfHP1 (Scherf et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a review.

claim: H4K31me1 enrichment was detected, although unevenly and at low rates, in the vicinity of few var (5 out of 64) and rifin genes.
source: H4K31me1 enrichment was detected, although unevenly and at low rates, in the vicinity of few var (5 out of 64) and rifin genes (Figure 12c).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 12c.

claim: The lack of spread of H4K31me1 along a series of nucleosomes may be explained by the absence of a competent protein reader that specifically recognizes the PTM and recruits the H4K31me1-catalyzing methyltransferase.
source: The lack of spread of H4K31me1 along a series of nucleosomes may be explained by the absence of a competent protein reader that specifically recognizes the PTM and recruits the H4K31me1-catalyzing methyltransferase.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the observed limited spreading of H4K31me1.

claim: The bromodomain of BRD4 is able to recognize the acetylated isoform of H4K31.
source: In fact, the bromodomain of BRD4 is able to recognize the acetylated isoform of H4K31 (Filippakopoulos et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation.

claim: P. falciparum centromeres were originally described as displaying a unique epigenetic status typified by the noteworthy absence of the canonical pericentromeric PTM H3K9me3.
source: P. falciparum centromeres were originally described as displaying a unique epigenetic status typified by the noteworthy absence of the canonical pericentromeric PTM H3K9me3 (Hoeijmakers et al., 2012), which is present in all species including T. gondii (Figure 10c and Figure 10—figure supplement 4) (Brooks et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations and ChIP-seq data.

claim: This study has emphasized an unusual role of H4K31me1 in pericentromeric heterochromatin in P. falciparum.
source: Clearly this study has emphasized an unusual role of H4K31me1 in pericentromeric heterochromatin in P. falciparum and has provided new insights on the mechanism of transcriptional regulation in T. gondii.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the ChIP-seq data presented.

claim: In metazoans, H4K31me1 was shown to decorate the mitotic chromosome arms.
source: In metazoans, H4K31me1 was shown to decorate the mitotic chromosome arms (Figure 7b).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7b.

claim: H4K31me1 is a novel mitotic marker that targets newly synthesized H4 that may be involved in the regulation of chromosomal condensation and segregation during mitosis.
source: In this regard, H4K31me1 is a novel mitotic marker that targets newly synthesized H4 that may be involved in the regulation of chromosomal condensation and segregation during mitosis.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the observed localization of H4K31me1 on mitotic chromosomes.

claim: H4K31 is structurally very close to H3K56.
source: H4K31 is structurally very close to H3K56 (Figure 1c), the acetylation of which is reported to increase the binding affinity of H3 toward histone chaperones, thereby promoting nucleosome assembly during the S phase of the cell cycle (Li et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 1c and a citation.

claim: H4K31 methylation, unlike H3K56ac, is predicted to prevent histone exchange, thereby slowing histone turnover rate behind the replication forks.
source: However, the picture appears more complex than this as H4K31 methylation, unlike H3K56ac, is predicted to prevent histone exchange, thereby slowing histone turnover rate behind the replication forks, which overall contributes to the stabilization of newly incorporated nucleosomes in chromatin.
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on the predicted effects of H4K31 methylation.

claim: H4K31 acetylation and methylation are associated with very distinct nuclear functions in T. gondii and P. falciparum.
source: In conclusion, we demonstrate that H4K31 acetylation and methylation are associated with very distinct nuclear functions in T. gondii and P. falciparum.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The study demonstrates the evolution of distinct epigenetic strategies to organize chromosome regions that are essential for cell division and gene expression in apicomplexan parasites.
source: Moreover, we demonstrate the evolution of distinct epigenetic strategies to organize chromosome regions that are essential for cell division and gene expression in apicomplexan parasites.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the comparative analysis of H4K31 modifications in T. gondii and P. falciparum.
